related_resources.reason: Detailed biography and family dates, education, Bateson, expeditions, institute and imprisonment; compare conflicting chronology with specialist studies.
Vavilov and Bateson, seed collection scale and international research links, wartime protection. Institutional commemoration.
Primary scientific argument; June 4, 1920 Saratov talk, 1922 English article and bounds of analogy.
Vavilov 1926 paper, revised geography, collection method, crop centers and modern impact.
Modern limits of the center-of-origin approach; archaeological and genetic complications, multiple domestications.
Living collections, accessions, ex-situ conservation, breeding programs, institutional holdings and management.
The scientific and breeding relevance of crop wild relatives and local varieties; conservation of genetic variation.
Russian archives establish institutional political threats predating Lysenko dominant power; pre-arrest repression.
Vernalization, claims beyond physiology, Lysenko political ascent, personnel purges, 1939 denunciation, 1948 academy meeting.
Expeditions, institute plant varieties, siege-era collection preservation; wartime staff accounts are retrospective.
Bateson training, career, international recognition; member elected June 1942 while prisoner; brief archive narrative has an erroneous prison location.
International collection contacts, years of imprisonment and seed conservation history.
1940 arrest during western-Ukraine expedition, Saratov death, academy career, posthumous rehabilitation.
Discussion of politically coerced agronomy, Vavilov arrest and transfer, survival and later history of VIR. Interpret archival claims cautiously.
Barulina as biologist and geneticist, relationship, scholarly work, absent personal correspondence; no private dialogue inferred.
VIR institutional history, 1934 Vavilov qualified support for vernalization and later critical dispute; specialist historical compilation.
History of crop collection and preservation with archival imagery; context for global conservation.
